name: Generic Consumer
helpText:
Implement the Consumer interface to connect a custom source. The downstream payload type depends on your implementation; Studio cannot infer it.

ESB flows, including demos, must remain running and ready for later input after the initial sample batch. Prefer correctly scheduled, polling or listener-based input. For a custom or event-generating source, implement pacing, cancellation, rollback and stop/start against the selected framework version. Do not fake isRunning, busy-spin, suppress failures or flood output.

Verify first delivery, continued readiness during idle time, and a later batch in the same running application without bean reset or flow/application restart. Finite completion is only appropriate for explicitly requested batch examples or bounded tests; a README or completion message does not excuse an unexpectedly Stopped ESB flow.
allowableProperties_comment: Note that the order of properties in this file dictates the order displayed on screen, unless propertyDisplayOrder is set, which will be used as the primary key

componentName.helpText: The name of the component as displayed on diagrams. The name should be unique for the flow. The name will be used internally to reflect the bean created.

configuration.helpText: Provide the bean type that contains bespoke configurations for this component.
configuration.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the Configuration bean.

configurationId.helpText: By default, the configuration ID is moduleName + flowName + componentName + componentType. Override it when multiple flows should share a configuration, or when renaming a flow without changing configuration already stored in the override-properties database.

requiresStub.helpText: Does this component require a stub to be generated by Studio, if not, it is assumed the user will provide the instance from its own factory class.

userImplementedClassName.helpText: The name of the class that that implements the interface for this generic component.
userImplementedClassName.validationMessage: Provide a valid java classname for the consumer e.g. starting with upper case, followed by number/characters etc.
